What is UCEED Entrance Exam?

Undergraduate Common Entrance Examination for Design (UCEED) is a national-level exam conducted by IIT Bombay for admission to the B.Des program at the following institutes: IIT Bombay , IIT Delhi , IIT Guwahati , IIT Hyderabad , and IIITDM Jabalpur . The UCEED exam is conducted once every year, usually in January. In the previous edition of the exam, more than 15,000 candidates registered for the exam, out of which around 13,500 candidates appeared in the exam.

Admission is based on UCEED merit . The candidate has to appear in the UCEED entrance exam , which is conducted by IIT Bombay. Merit lists for admission are prepared considering the marks of UCEED 2026. Also, the scores will be used to shortlist candidates for counseling. UCEED scores are also used by result-sharing institutes. However, the result-sharing institutes will use UCEED 2026 scores to fill available seats in their UG courses.

UCEED 2026 is expected to be offered in seven institutes: IIT Bombay (IITB), IIT Delhi (IITD), IIT Guwahati (IITG), IIT Hyderabad (IITH), IIT Indore (IITI), IIT Roorkee (IITR), and IIITDM Jabalpur (IIITDMJ). IIT Bombay will process the common application form and conduct the joint seat allocation process for UCEED 2026.

blocks.value: UCEED 2026 Cut-off

IIT Bombay released the UCEED cutoff marks for Part A on February 05, 2026. The cut-offs are released in the form of mean and standard deviation . Only such candidates who meet the cut-off will be considered for admission to the B.Des program offered by the participating colleges of IIT Bombay. Candidates who are higher in the merit rank will be allocated seats first. Part B answer booklets will be evaluated only if the candidate meets the Part A cut-off marks . The mean and standard deviation for Part-A (UCEED 2026) are 70.86 and 25.77.

Marks obtained in Part-A will be used to shortlist candidates. The cut-off (𝛿) for Part-A marks to shortlist candidates in the OPEN category will be 𝜇 + (𝜎⁄2) = 𝛿, where 𝜇 and 𝜎 are the average marks and standard deviation of distribution of marks obtained by ALL the candidates in Part-A of UCEED 2026 . The 𝜇, 𝜎, and 𝛿 will be rounded off to two decimal places. The candidates belonging to the reserved categories shall have to fulfil a relaxed cut-off mark, which will be 0.9𝛿 for OBC-NCL/EWS, 0.5𝛿 for SC/ST/PwD, where 𝛿 is the cut-off mark for the OPEN category.

blocks.value: The evaluation of Part-B will be done manually by at least two expert evaluators separately and independently. Following is the scheme of evaluation for each question in Part-B.

value: If the difference in marks awarded by the two evaluators <= 10 marks, a simple average of the two evaluations will be considered.
If the difference > 10 marks, the answer sheet of Part-B will be evaluated by a third expert examiner (and so on until the difference of marks <= 10).
A simple average of the closest of two evaluations will be selected as the final marks.
If the difference in marks of the closest of two evaluations is >10 after several evaluations, a moderator will be invited to examine the answers.
If the difference in marks between the moderator and either of the examiners is the same, then the higher average will be considered for calculating the score.

faqs.question: What is evaluation process for UCEED 2026 Part B?
faqs.answer: The evaluation of Part-B will be done manually by at least two expert evaluators separately and independently. Following is the scheme of evaluation for each question in Part-B. If the difference in marks awarded by the two evaluators <= 10 marks, a simple average of the two evaluations will be considered. If the difference > 10 marks, the answer sheet of Part-B will be evaluated by a third expert examiner (and so on until the difference of marks <= 10). A simple average of the closest of two evaluations will be selected as the final marks. If the difference in marks of the closest of two evaluations is >10 after several evaluations, a moderator will be invited to examine the answers. If the difference in marks between the moderator and either of the examiners is the same, then the higher average will be considered for calculating the score.

UCEED 2026 cut-off will be available for all candidates who have appeared in the national-level design entrance exam. IIT Bombay will release the cut-off in the form of mean and standard deviations. The mean and standard deviation for Part-A (UCEED 2026) are 70.86 and 25.77 , respectively. The UCEED 2025 Part-A has a mean score of 61.50 and a standard deviation of 25.69 .

The candidate needs to check the cut-off for their applied category and their admission chances. It is mandatory to meet the cut-off, or else the candidate will be out of the race for admission. The qualifying cutoff is prepared by considering UCEED 2026 Part A marks. Candidates securing the cutoff marks will have their Part B paper evaluated. Candidates who meet the cut-off will be issued UCEED 2026 merit ranks . The admission cut-off for UCEED 2026, as the name suggests, will be released at the time of admission. It is the minimum mark a candidate needs to secure in the UCEED 2026 exam to be considered for seat allotment and admission. Also, the admission cutoff will be released for all the participating colleges. The scorecard for UCEED 2026 will be available for download from March 10, 2026 .
UCEED 2026 Part-A Cut-off Calculation

Marks obtained in UCEED Part-A will be used to shortlist candidates. The cut-off (𝛿) for Part-A marks to shortlist candidates in the OPEN category will be 𝜇 + (𝜎⁄2) = 𝛿, where 𝜇 and 𝜎 are the average marks and standard deviation of distribution of marks obtained by ALL the candidates in Part-A of UCEED 2026. The 𝜇, 𝜎, and 𝛿 will be rounded-off to two decimal places. The candidates belonging to the reserved categories shall have to fulfil a relaxed cut-off mark, which will be 0.9𝛿 for OBC-NCL/EWS, 0.5𝛿 for SC/ST/PwD, where 𝛿 is the cut-off mark for the Open category.
IIT UCEED 2026 Cut-off Formula

value: General/Open Category: Mean + (Z × Standard Deviation) = 61.50 + (0.2 × 25.69) = 66.63 (Rounded to 100 for the final cut-off)

faqs.question: What are the salient features of best books for CEED?
faqs.answer: Here are some of the important traits of CEED best books. These books will be written in layman terms and explain the concepts lucidly. Contain few to no errors. They will also be as per the latest and revised CEED syllabus. They will also have enough problem sets, typically at the end of each chapter, that the candidate can practice and thus hone their problem-solving skills and better understand the concepts. faqs.question: Can I depend only on CEED books to prepare for the exam?
faqs.answer: Simply relying on textbooks for CEED exam preparation is not enough. It is because the CEED exam will evaluate the conceptual understanding of the candidate and also whether they are able to use those concepts to solve various types of problems. So, along with the textbooks, the candidate also need to solve sample papers. In fact, the candidate can start solving sample papers very early on in their preparation. Further, mock tests are another great tool to fine tune one’s preparation; mocks, however, unlike sample papers, are meant to be taken closer to the exam.

faqs.question: What are various other resources, other than books that I can use to prepare for CEED Entrance exam?
faqs.answer: While text books should be the primary resource for CEED Entrance exam preparation, there are other resources candidate may use effectively. For example, YouTube has many educational and preparation videos that candidate can refer to. To identify quality and genuineness (or correctness) of the data, you can go through the video reviews. In some cases, review section may be hidden. In that case, you better stay away, as it is difficult to find the quality of the content.

faqs.question: What should I do if I am finding a CEED topic difficult and not able to complete?
faqs.answer: You can give a few attempts. But after that, move on to the next topic. Don’t spend too much time on one simple topic because you will run out of time and will not be able to complete the syllabus. Leave that topic and try to study at the end if you have ample time left.

faqs.question: Is the CEED exam tough?
faqs.answer: The difficulty level of CEED exam has been maintained by authorities over the years. However, most design aspirants share that if difficulty level of all design entrance exams conducted for PG level courses is compared then CEED is slightly easier than NID Entrance Exam. This is primarily because the drawing questions asked in NID that are considered to be tougher than those put forth in CEED exam. Note that CEED exam is for admission to the M.Des courses offered by the eight participating colleges. Meanwhile, the NID that for the M.Des programme has three participating colleges.
